papers.title: A Well-Separated Pair Decomposition of Linear Size for Unit-Disk Graphs
papers.abstract: We prove that every connected Euclidean-weighted unit-disk graph on $n$ vertices has a $(1/\varepsilon)$-well-separated pair decomposition of size $O(n\varepsilon^{-2}\log(1/\varepsilon))$. This resolves an open problem posed by Gao and Zhang in 2003. We also show that this bound is tight: there are connected unit-disk graphs for which any $(1/\varepsilon)$-well-separated pair decomposition has size $\Omega(n\varepsilon^{-2}\log (1/\varepsilon))$.

papers.title: The computational complexity of Undirected Vertex Geography with maximum height 3
papers.abstract: The impartial game Undirected Vertex Geography is known to be polynomial time solvable. The variant in which vertices are assigned heights with maximum value m that reduce by 1 whenever the token is moved from that vertex, denoted UIRm, is known to be polynomial time solvable when m=2 and PSPACE-complete when m=4. We solve the open question of the computational complexity of UIR3 by a reduction from Directed vertex geography, and show that the complexity holds when the underlying graph is planar and (a) has degree at most 3, (b) is bipartite with maximum degree 4, or (c) is bipartite with maximum degree 5 and only has heights of 1 and 3.

papers.title: Goemans's Unsplittable-Flow Conjecture: The Anatomy of AI-Assisted Counterexample Discovery
papers.abstract: Goemans conjectured that any fractional single-source flow could be converted into an unsplittable flow without increasing total cost and while increasing any arc load by at most the largest demand. Recently, Dmitry Rybin announced a seven-vertex counterexample found through an interaction with ChatGPT, which disproved this long-standing conjecture. However, the interaction did not reveal why this particular topology and its demand, fractional-flow, and cost choices work together, whether the example belongs to a broader family, or which structural features determine where counterexamples can occur. It also left unclear why the AI-assisted search succeeded where earlier human efforts had not. In this paper, we develop a forward counterexample construction pipeline. It starts from an arborescence on which failure is impossible and adds terminal-entering shortcut arcs. The resulting load constraints define a finite set of admissible route choices; their convex hull, the conflict polytope, yields exact conditions for demands, fractional flows, and costs. Starting from a simple arborescence, the pipeline selects Rybin's topology and characterizes all counterexamples it supports. Experiments further demonstrate the pipeline's transferability: when instructed to follow it while varying the initial arborescence and shortcut placement, ChatGPT produced counterexamples on topologies genuinely different from Rybin's and found valid constructions starting from 93 other rooted arborescence shapes. The theory also explains why the original example was difficult to discover through blind enumeration and suggests that Rybin's interaction lies between blind enumeration and a complete theory-guided construction.

papers.title: Faster polynomial-space algorithms for poset problems
papers.abstract: We give a polynomial-space, deterministic, exact algorithm for counting linear extensions of partial orders over $n$ elements, with running time $O^*((2\sqrt{2})^{n}) \subseteq O(2.829^n)$. This improves upon the long-standing bound of $O^*(4^{n})$ attainable by standard divide and conquer (Savitch 1970, Gurevich and Shelah 1987). Our algorithm uses a similar balanced splitting approach as the classical algorithm, but applies it only to the elements outside a largest antichain. For the elements of the antichain itself we develop a formula based on inclusion-exclusion that accounts for the ways in which they can appear in a linear extension. The technique is also applicable to other problems on posets, which we illustrate by solving the well-studied jump number problem in a similar running time of $O^*((2\sqrt{2})^{n})$ and polynomial space. To our knowledge, these are the first polynomial-space algorithms with a running time below $4^n$ for both problems.

papers.title: Classification of Forbidden 0-1 Patterns by Their Extremal Function
papers.abstract: This paper concerns the maximum weight of $n\times n$ 0-1 matrices that avoid some pattern $P$, denoted $\operatorname{ex}(n,P)$. Furedi and Hajnal initiated a research program of classifying all patterns according to their extremal function, but to date, only the weight-4 patterns are completely understood. In this paper we make progress on several fronts of the classification problem. A pattern is light if its columns have weight 1 and linear if $\operatorname{ex}(n,P)=O(n)$. We characterize the set of weight-5 linear light patterns, and the set of weight-5 linear patterns more generally. Along the way we identify several new infinite classes of linear patterns, which support the Pettie-Tardos conjecture on characterizing all linear light patterns. It was known that there exist infinitely many minimally nonlinear patterns. We identify a specific infinite set of minimally nonlinear patterns. We also prove that there are $2^{\Omega(r)}$ weight-$r$ minimally nonlinear patterns, and that every minimally nonlinear pattern has extremal function $O(n\log n)$, with the exception of the 4-cycle. We classify many of the outstanding weight-5 patterns according to their extremal function, leaving only a small set remaining. The newly classified weight-5 patterns have extremal function $\Theta(n)$ or $\Theta(n\alpha(n))$. We also exhibit a large number of weight-6 patterns with extremal function $\Theta(n\log n/\log\log n)$, which is notable in that this function had not been encountered before for any single pattern $P$, though it was known to be the correct extremal function for a pair of forbidden patterns.

papers.title: An additive-square-free word over an alphabet of size 6
papers.abstract: An additive square over $\mathbb{N}$ is two consecutive nonempty blocks of the same length and same sum. For example, 1423 is an additive square, since 14 and 23 both have length 2 and sum 5. Solving a problem that has been open for more than 50 years, we give an example of an infinite word over a 6-letter subset of N that avoids additive squares.

papers.title: A combinatorial proof of a symmetric joint distribution on strict binary trees
papers.abstract: Nonplanar strict binary trees on $2n+1$ vertices are enumerated by the reduced tangent numbers $T_{2n+1}/2^n$, whose entries are refined by Poupard's triangle. Poupard defined the end of the minimal chain ($\mathrm{eoc}$) and the parent of the maximum leaf ($\mathrm{pom}$) on these trees, proving that $\mathrm{eoc}$ and $\mathrm{pom}+1$ share this triangular distribution. Foata and Han subsequently showed via tree calculus and partial difference equations that the joint distribution of $(\mathrm{eoc}, 2n+1-\mathrm{pom})$ is symmetric. By introducing an auxiliary tree statistic dual to $\mathrm{eoc}$, we give a bijective proof of this symmetry. Our proof composes a recursive bijection on strict binary trees, a bijection to alternating Andr\'e permutations, and the reverse-complement involution on permutations.

papers.title: Treewidth 3 in the Product Structure Theorem for Bounded Degree Graphs in Minor-Closed Classes
papers.abstract: We show that, for all positive integers $t$ and $\Delta$, there exists an integer $c$ such that, for every $K_t$-minor-free graph $G$ with maximum degree at most $\Delta$, there exists a graph $H$ of treewidth at most $3$ and a path $P$ such that $G$ is isomorphic to a subgraph of the strong product $H\boxtimes P\boxtimes K_c$. This improves on a previous result of Dujumovi\'c, Esperet, Micek, Walczak, and Wood (2022) by bounding the treewidth of $H$ independently of $t$ and $\Delta$. As an immediate consequence we obtain a bound of $O(r^4)$ on the $r$-weak colouring number of bounded-degree graphs from any proper minor-closed graph class.

papers.title: List packing for graphs with small arboricity
papers.abstract: We prove that every graph $G$ whose edge set is the union of $r$ forests has list packing number at most $2^r$. This means that for all $k\ge 2^r$ and every list-assignment $L$ with lists of size $k$, the graph $G$ admits $k$ disjoint proper $L$-colourings. While for large $r$ this bound is far from optimal, for $r\in\{1,2\}$ it is sharp. As a direct corollary of the case $r=2$, we obtain that every triangle-free planar graph has list packing number at most $4$, thus improving upon a result of Dvo\v{r}\'ak, Masa\v{r}\'ik, Mus\'ilek and Pangr\'ac and providing the optimal answer to a question of Dvo\v{r}\'ak, Postle and Norin on (weighted) $\epsilon$-flexibility of such graphs. As a corollary of the case $r=3$, we obtain a short alternative proof that every $K_5$-minor-free (and hence every planar) graph has list-packing number at most $8$, matching the state of the art. All results above also hold for the stronger notion of correspondence packing.

papers.title: Increasing arc-connectivity by bounded- and fixed-size inversions
papers.abstract: For a digraph $D$ and some $X \subseteq V(D)$, the inversion of $X$ is the operation of flipping all arcs both of whose endvertices are in $X$. We initiate the study of establishing arc-connectivity properties by applying inversions of bounded or fixed size. For fixed-size inversions, the feasibility problem is interesting. For all integers $p \geq 2$ and $k \geq 1$, we give a characterization of the digraphs that can be made $k$-arc-strong by applying inversions of size exactly $p$, provided they are sufficiently large. For bounded-size inversions, the feasibility problem is easy, so we focus on minimising the number of inversions. We prove that for all integers $p\geq 3$ and $k \geq 1$ and any $\epsilon>0$, there exists a polynomial-time $(4k-2+\epsilon)$-approximation algorithm for computing the minimum number of inversions of size at most $p$ that make a given digraph $k$-arc-strong. This is in stark contrast to other results on inversion optimization problems. On the other hand, we show that for any $p\geq 3$ and $k \geq 1$ the problem is NP-hard, and, moreover, APX-hard. As a result on parameterized complexity, we show that for any $k \geq 2$, it is $W[1]$-hard with respect to $p$ to decide whether a given digraph can be made $k$-arc-strong by applying a single inversion of size at most $p$. We also prove that for a given multidigraph, it is $W[1]$-hard with respect to $\ell$ to decide whether it can be made 2-arc-strong by applying $\ell$ inversions of size 2.

papers.title: Subword enumeration up to stack-sorting equivalence
papers.abstract: Defant and Kravitz introduced generalizations of West's stack-sorting map $s$ from permutations to finite words. This raises questions as to how such generalizations could be applied in the field of combinatorics on words. The Defant-Kravitz generalizations of $s$ depend on how repeated occurrences of the same character within a word may be repositioned, according to their $\textsf{tortoise}$ and $\textsf{hare}$ operations. As demonstrated in this paper, these operations provide a natural way of extending abelian complexity functions for infinite sequences, in a way that gives light to structural properties associated with infinite words. We apply these new ideas to two famous infinite words: the paperfolding word and the Thue-Morse word. In the case of the Thue-Morse word, we discover an interesting connection to the previous work of several authors, such as de Luca and Varricchio, on the ``special'' factors of the Thue-Morse word. This may be seen as providing a basis for a new and interdisciplinary area linking the combinatorics about the stack-sorting of permutations with the field of combinatorics on words.

papers.title: Semifields and rank-metric codes from Drinfeld modules
papers.abstract: We establish a connection between Drinfeld modules and rank-metric codes, focusing on maximum rank distance codes arising from finite semifields. Our method constructs rank-metric codes from linear subspaces of endomorphisms of a Drinfeld module acting on torsion submodules. Using a duality between a Drinfeld module and its endomorphisms, we show that Sheekey's construction fits naturally into this framework, yielding a short conceptual proof of his main theorem. Next, to demonstrate the potential of our method, we construct, for every prime power $q$, new semifields of order $q^9$, which are distinguished from the known ones by their nuclear parameters. Finally, going beyond the Drinfeld module $\phi_T=\tau^n$ that underlies Sheekey's and related constructions, we obtain infinite families of semifield codes from Drinfeld modules with smaller endomorphism rings, and show that the corresponding semifields are cyclic semifields of Petit.

papers.title: Dessins d'Enfants as a Topological Lens on Temporal Hypergraphs
papers.abstract: Hypergraphs are the natural language for group interactions, and topological data analysis has given us several ways to look at them: simplicial and cell complexes, persistent homology, and sheaves. All of these treat a hyperedge as an unordered set. In this paper, we introduce a different and, to our knowledge, new viewpoint that comes from Grothendieck's theory of dessins d'enfants and, unlike these approaches, takes into account the order in which vertices appear in each hyperedge and hyperedges appear around each vertex. A dessin is a bipartite graph drawn on a closed orientable surface. Through Walsh's classical correspondence between hypermaps and bipartite maps, every hypergraph equipped with a cyclic order of incidences at each vertex and inside each hyperedge is a dessin, and therefore determines a surface with faces and a genus. We develop this idea for temporal hypergraphs and build the surface by replaying history: incidences are added in the order in which they occurred, and each new incidence is inserted into the cyclic orders built so far, next to the earlier incidence to which it is related. We prove that every insertion either grows the hypergraph without creating a cycle, closes a cycle locally by splitting a face, or closes it globally by adding a handle; the number of independent cycles equals the number of local plus handle events, and the genus equals the number of handle events. These counts give interpretable, size-controlled measures of how a temporal hypergraph's cycles organize on a surface as it grows. We apply our method to five Stack Exchange communities and show that it separates communities that standard statistics cannot tell apart and quantifies how much the real order of interactions matters. We further discuss what the surface viewpoint adds to existing higher-order network analysis and how it opens a path toward dessin-based learning on hypergraphs.

papers.title: Ramsey Theory for Edge Ideals
papers.abstract: We initiate the study of Ramsey theory for edge ideals. The edge ideal I_G is generated by the monomials x_ux_v for all edges uv of G. A central invariant measuring structure in algebraic geometry and commutative algebra are the betti number beta_{i,j}(S/I) for some ideal I in a ring S. We prove the Ramsey Theorem for Edge Ideals: For any betti number indices i,j, and any number of colors m, there is a graph F such that for every m-coloring of the edges of F, there is a color l such that beta_{i,j}(S/I_{F_l}) >0, where F_l is the subgraph of F whose edges are in color l. Moreover, the number of vertices of F is at most jm^2.

papers.title: Singularities of ideals with minimal tangent space dimension in the Hilbert scheme of points on a threefold
papers.abstract: We classify all singular monomial ideals in the Hilbert scheme of $d$ points on $\mathbb{A}^3$ whose tangent spaces have the minimal dimension $3d+6$. There are two families called the opera houses and rotating staircases, and we give their combinatorial and algebraic descriptions. All the opera houses are in one linkage class, and their singularities are smoothly equivalent to the vertex of a cone over the Grassmannian $\mathrm{Gr}(2,6) \hookrightarrow \mathbb{P}^{14}$ in its Pl\"ucker embedding. The rotating staircases split into many linkage classes and we give some examples.

papers.title: On the asymmetry polynomial of Schubert varieties
papers.abstract: Let $W$ be a finite Weyl group with length function $\ell$ and longest element $w_0$. For $w\in W$, let $P_w(q)$ be the Poincar\'e polynomial of the Schubert variety $X_w$. We introduce its asymmetry polynomial $D_w(q):=q^{\ell(w)}P_w(q^{-1})-P_w(q)$. Let $n\geq4$ and $W=S_n$ or $W(B_n)$. For $w\in W$ whose Kazhdan--Lusztig polynomial $P_{\mathrm{id},w}(q)$ satisfies $P_{\mathrm{id},w}(1)=2$, we prove the sharp bound $[q^k]D_w(q)\leq[q^{k-1}]P_{w_0}(q)$ for $1\leq k<\ell(w)/2$. For every $n\geq3$ and $1\leq h\leq2n-4$, we construct an element $b=b_h^n\in W(B_n)$ with $P_{\mathrm{id},b}(q)=1+q^h$, and determine the asymmetry polynomial $D_b(q)$ and all Kazhdan--Lusztig polynomials $P_{x,b}(q)$ for $x\leq b$.

papers.title: Partial flags of tropical linear spaces may not complete
papers.abstract: We construct two valuated matroids of ranks 2 and 4 on eight elements that form a valuated quotient, such that no rank 3 valuated matroid forms a valuated quotient with both simultaneously. In other words, a partial flag of tropical linear spaces need not extend to a complete flag containing every intermediate dimension.

papers.title: Tropical Geometry of $G_2$
papers.abstract: We tropicalize the Grassmannian and the flag variety of the algebraic group of type $G_2$. The two tropical varieties are strictly contained in the associated Dressians. Their points are trees in the $G_2$-forest and decorated trees in the $G_2$-orchard. These form hexagons in incidence geometry. We classify all toric degenerations and their Newton-Okounkov polytopes. Mukai theory leads us to tropical canonical curves of genus 10. This article serves as a blueprint for studies of reductive groups in tropical geometry.

papers.title: Affine extensions and central compression for product-one-free sequences
papers.abstract: Let $H_s=H_{27}\times C_3^s$, where $H_{27}$ is the nonabelian group of order $27$ and exponent three. We study the elements which can be adjoined to a product-one-free sequence $L$ of length $2s+5$. Let $Q$ be its central subsequence and let $h$ be the dimension of the subgroup generated by $Q$. If $2h-|Q|\le1$, all admissible individual extensions lie in one affine hyperplane of the full additive group coordinates, avoiding the identity. The proof combines coefficient identities with finite, explicitly verified configurations and a transfer valid in every dimension. We also prove an exact central compression theorem: a central zero-sum-free block of length $2h-1$ can be replaced by one term after quotienting by an $(h-1)$-dimensional central subgroup, with a forward implication for product-one-freeness and admissible extensions. For the extraspecial group $E_2$ of order $3^5$ and exponent three, a finite stress obstruction and central compression yield a further uniform restriction: in any product-one-free sequence of length $2r+11$ over $E_2\times C_3^r$, the central subsequence is nonempty and has length at most $2h-2$, where $h$ is its full central rank.

papers.title: Log-concavity for alternating Eulerian polynomials
papers.abstract: Alternating Eulerian polynomials enumerate permutations by the alternating descent statistic introduced by Chebikin. We prove that their coefficient sequences are log-concave, verifying a conjecture of Lin, Ma, Wang and Wang. Our proof combines a factorization involving reciprocal quadratic factors, estimates for ordinary Eulerian zeros, and a log-concavity criterion for products of such factors. The required finite verifications use exact integer arithmetic. As applications, we obtain log-concavity for the distribution of $3$-descents, a local limit theorem for alternating descents, and bounds for the largest coefficient. We also give a Lorentzian reformulation of the main theorem.

papers.title: Local connectivity of friends-and-strangers graphs with a star
papers.abstract: Given two finite simple graphs $X$ and $Y$ with the same number of vertices, the vertex set of the friends-and-strangers graph $\FS(X,Y)$ consists of all bijections from the vertices of $X$ to the vertices of $Y$. Two bijections are adjacent exactly when one is obtained from the other by swapping the images of two adjacent vertices of $X$, while leaving all other images unchanged, and the two swapped images are adjacent in $Y$. For $n\ge2$, let $\Star_n$ be the star on $n$ vertices. Krishnan and Li [Electron. J. Combin. 33 (2026), no. 3, Paper P3.41] conjectured that, for $n\ge3$, whenever $\FS(X,\Star_n)$ is connected, the maximum number of pairwise internally vertex-disjoint paths between any two distinct vertices is equal to the smaller of their degrees. We prove this conjecture. More precisely, if $\FS(X,\Star_n)$ is connected, then $X$ must be $2$-connected, and the conjectured equality holds for every pair of distinct vertices. We further prove the stronger result that, whenever $X$ is $2$-connected, the same equality holds in every connected component of $\FS(X,\Star_n)$.

papers.title: Longitudinal Subdivision Invariance of Periodic Directed Strips and Its Application to Elongated Octagonal Strips
papers.abstract: We prove that longitudinal refinements of finite-width periodic directed strips preserve subdivision containment. The refinement lengths may be arbitrary positive integers, without a uniform upper bound, and no matching condition is imposed on the horizontal arcs. We construct subdivision models in both directions that preserve each designated rail as a whole. The equivalence also holds when the designated rail images are required to lie in a prescribed end. A nonperiodic example shows that reverse containment may fail without periodicity. As an application, we obtain an elongated octagonal strip $O_n$ by subdividing selected longitudinal arcs of the directed hexagonal strip $H_n$. We show that every bounded face of $O_n$ is an octagon for $n\geq 2$ and that $O_n$ and $H_n$ are subdivision-equivalent. Consequently, the known exact end in-degree thresholds and forced-width formula for $H_n$ also hold for $O_n$.

papers.title: An Explicit Construction of Large Families of MSTD Sets
papers.abstract: A finite set $S\subset\mathbb Z$ is more sums than differences (MSTD) if $|S+S|>|S-S|$. Yufei Zhao's bidirectional-ballot construction gives $\Theta(2^N/N)$ MSTD subsets of $[0,N-1]$, the best previously known size bound for an explicit family, to the author's knowledge. We improve this bound: for every fixed integer $T\geq1$, we construct a family of $\Theta_T(2^N/(\log_2^{\circ T} N)^{2^T})$ MSTD subsets, where $\log_2^{\circ T}$ denotes the $T$-fold iterated logarithm. This family is asymptotically larger than Zhao's for every fixed $T\geq1$. A subfamily of the same order of magnitude can be numbered so that any chosen member can be generated deterministically in time polynomial in $N$, without listing preceding members. As a supplementary comparison, replacing the terminal ballot rule by exhaustive fringe search gives a positive-proportion family with the same polynomial-time generation property.

papers.title: Non-principality of forbidden subposet problems
papers.abstract: We show pairs of posets such that the largest families not containing any of them is substantially smaller than the largest families avoiding only one of them.

papers.title: Antidirected paths on five vertices in 5-chromatic digraphs
papers.abstract: We prove that every 5-chromatic digraph containing no copy of the regular tournament on five vertices contains both antidirected paths on five vertices. This answers a question posed by El Sahili in 2004. The proof uses an edge bound for 5-critical graphs to constrain the out-degrees in a counterexample and obtain a contradiction by constructing a proper 4-colouring.

papers.title: Minimal super dominating sets of maximum cardinality
papers.abstract: Let $G = (V,E)$ be a graph. A subset $S \subseteq V$ of vertices is a super dominating set if every vertex $v \in V - S$ has a neighbour $u \in S$, whose only neighbour in $V - S$ is $v$. A set $S \subseteq V$ is called open irredundant if every vertex $u \in S$ has at least one neighbour $v \in V - S$ whose only neighbour in $S$ is $u$. In this paper we establish connections between super dominating sets and open irredundant sets, similar to the connections that exist between dominating sets and irredundant sets. In particular, we define the new parameter $\Gamma _{sp}(G)$ as the maximum cardinality of a minimal super dominating set of $G$ and calculate $\Gamma _{sp}(G)$ for some families of graphs $G$. Finally we present some properties of open irredundant sets and we will develop Gallai theorems involving domination, super domination and open irredundance parameters of graphs.

papers.title: Unique-maximum colourings of planar graphs with respect to neighbourhoods
papers.abstract: A colouring of the vertices of a graph by positive integers is a unique-maximum colouring with respect to open (resp. closed) neighbourhoods if the maximum colour appears exactly once in the open (resp. closed) neighbourhood of every vertex. Fabrici, Lu\v{z}ar, Rindo\v{s}ov\'a and Sot\'ak (Discrete Appl. Math. 324 (2023) 80-92) conjectured that four colours suffice for closed neighbourhoods in planar graphs. We prove this conjecture by colouring a suitable independent dominating set with the three largest colours. They further conjectured that six colours suffice if the colouring is also proper. We disprove this conjecture by a planar graph which needs seven colours, and we show that seven colours always suffice. For open neighbourhoods, we show that eight colours suffice, even for proper colourings, which improves the previous bound of ten. In the proper case, our graph again needs seven colours. If the colouring need not be proper and the graph has no vertices of degree 2, then six colours suffice.

papers.title: Binomially Weighted Partition Statistics: Generating Functions, Asymptotics, and Dominance
papers.abstract: For an integer partition $\lambda=(\lambda_1,\lambda_2,\ldots)$, we consider $M_m(\lambda)=\sum_{i\geq1}\binom{i+m}{m+1}\lambda_i$, where $m\geq0$. We prove conjugation and Frobenius-coordinate identities for this family and obtain its ordinary and bivariate generating functions. Differentiating the bivariate product gives exact formulas for the mean and variance under uniform sampling of partitions of $n$. For fixed $m$, we show that $\mathbb E[M_m]\sim\zeta(m+3)(\sqrt{6n}/\pi)^{m+3}$ and determine an explicit positive constant multiplying $(\sqrt{6n}/\pi)^{2m+5}$ in the variance asymptotic. The family encompasses the row sum underlying the discrete Gini statistic and, after conjugation, a linear combination giving the Wiener index of starlike trees; the associated normalized statistics have contrasting limits under uniform random sampling. We also prove that every $M_m$ is strictly decreasing along the dominance order. Consequently its level sets are antichains, providing coefficient-based lower bounds for the width of the dominance lattice.

papers.title: The Gini Index of an Integer Composition
papers.abstract: We extend the discrete Gini statistic on integer partitions to integer compositions by rearranging the parts in decreasing order. Under the uniform distribution on the $2^{n-1}$ compositions of $n$, the resulting statistic has a rational ordinary generating function for its aggregate values, as well as a rational generating function for its second moments. More generally, the generating function of every fixed raw moment is rational, although the bivariate generating function encoding the entire distribution is not. We obtain an exact formula for the mean and prove that the variance of the unnormalized statistic is asymptotic to $10n^3/189$. The normalization used for partitions has mean tending to $2/3$, in contrast to the limit $1$ under uniform random partitions. Using the separator representation of a random composition and a renewal-reward argument, we prove a central limit theorem: its centered, normalized Gini statistic has asymptotic Gaussian fluctuations with variance constant $40/189$. We also prove that the ordinary classical Gini coefficient of the composition parts tends to $1/3$ and satisfies a central limit theorem with variance constant $20/189$.

papers.title: 3-Cube-Free Sets in Cyclic Groups
papers.abstract: A set is called $3$-cube-free if it contains no configuration of the following form: $\{x,y,z,x+y,x+z,y+z,x+y+z\}$. We study the maximum density of $3$-cube-free sets in finite cyclic groups. As observed by Meng, every $3$-cube-free subset of $\mathbb Z_m$ has size at most $2m/3$, and this bound is sharp whenever $3\mid m$. Our main result shows that there exists an absolute constant $\varepsilon>0$ such that, for every $m$ not divisible by $3$, every $3$-cube-free subset of $\mathbb{Z}_m$ has size at most $\left(2/3-\varepsilon\right)m$. Thus, in this setting, the natural $2/3$ barrier can be uniformly improved. Long and Wagner conjectured that every $3$-cube-free subset of $\mathbb Z_{2^n}$ has size at most $5\cdot 2^n/8$. We also establish this conjecture for 3-cube-free sets whose density in the layer of odd residues is at least $2/3$. Together with induction, this reduces the conjecture to the case where this density lies in $(5/8,2/3)$.
